question: Do independently described Rarámuri varieties permit a passive-marked predicate to be closed by an external nominalizer, and what does that imply for complex forms such as Western newálime?

comparanda.source: Villalpando Quiñonez, Jesús. ¿Píri mu rimúli?: la narración de los sueños en el rarámuri de Norogachi. Tlalocan.
comparanda.translation_context: (el sueño) de los peces que son atrapados

comparanda.source: Compendio básico de la gramática ralámuli, 1997

structural_generalization.assessment: Two separately described varieties explicitly attest an outer nominalizer after passive morphology. This establishes the morphotactic availability of nominalizing an already complex passive predicate.

relevance_to_newalime.assessment: The bridge strengthens the structural plausibility of analyzing Western newálime as an internally complex predicate followed by an external -me/-ame nominalizing/participial element.

prohibited_inferences: Do not infer that Baja-TB -li and Norogachi -wa are historically the same morpheme.
Do not infer that -me and -ami are interchangeable in every Rarámuri variety or construction.
Do not use this structural parallel as a substitute for direct Western segmentation of newálime.
Do not treat the bridge as a sound law or cognacy proof.
next_tests: Find a same-root or tightly comparable paradigm contrasting Baja-TB -li-me with -wa-ami or -li-wa elsewhere.
Search additional Baja-TB texts for explicitly analyzable passive + nominalizer sequences.
Determine whether Western newálime has a published segmentation identifying the function of -li.
